parts: Please review /papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/research-overview/03_UNIFORM_ARITHMETIC_RESIDUAL_RESEARCH_PROGRAM_20261019.md and begin on the first task. Please update your progress in /symmetries/research-progress/02_UNIFORM_ARITHMETIC_RESIDUAL_PROGRESS_20261019.md and create a new summary document in /symmetries/summary to track progress on this new round of research.
I’ll read the research plan and repository workflow, begin the first task, and record the results in the progress log and a new round summary.

The first task is UAR-01: define the corrected residual and how it changes when a new arithmetic mode enters the cutoff. The existing work gives a fixed-height result and a separate scaling estimate, but their residuals differ. I’m checking that connection before choosing the new contract.

An earlier note already proves the leading edge’s cutoff-matching identity. That lets UAR-01 reuse established matching machinery and focus on the missing common contract: analytic domains, error terms, and a comparison norm. It does not yet supply the new uniform residual bound.

The draft now defines the corrected approximation, cutoff overlaps, and every signed transition in the interval-wide increment. The key distinction is explicit: cancellation within one chart does not by itself control an interval crossing many cutoffs. A separate reviewer is checking the contract’s signs, domains, and error ledger.

UAR-01 has passed the internal contract review. The checks cover transition signs, reflected contour notation, heat forcing, and error bookkeeping. I’m recording it as a contract milestone; the uniform estimates are still open. UAR-02 and UAR-03 can now begin from the same definitions and domains.

Completed [UAR-01’s reviewed residual and transition contract](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/notes/07_UAR01_CORRECTED_RESIDUAL_AND_TRANSITION_CONTRACT_20261019.md).

Updated the [progress register](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/research-progress/02_UNIFORM_ARITHMETIC_RESIDUAL_PROGRESS_20261019.md) and created the [new-round summary](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/summary/02_UNIFORM_ARITHMETIC_RESIDUAL_ROUND_SUMMARY_20261019.md).

Internal review and exact algebra/source checks passed. UAR-02 and UAR-03 are now ready; uniform estimates and new coverage remain open.
Please proceed with UAR-02
I’ll work on UAR-02’s uniform finite-mode remainder, then record the proof, checks, and any limits in the progress log and round summary.

The proof is taking shape. The prescribed correction appears to leave a finite-mode remainder of order \(x^{-2}\), even when the number of modes grows. I’m paying both Gaussian tails and the derivative cost before treating that as a usable result. The edge remainder remains a separate UAR-03 obligation.

The proof and outward checks have passed internal review. On the declared sector, the finite-mode remainder contributes less than \(1.9\times10^{-16}\) to the rotating first-jet error bound. That is a component bound: the retained correction, edge, and transitions still need to be combined. I’m saving the result and marking UAR-02 complete.

UAR-02 is complete. The [proof](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/03_normalized_jet_rotation/notes/08_UNIFORM_FINITE_GAMMA_HEAT_REMAINDER_20261019.md) establishes a uniform finite-mode remainder below \(2/c^2\), including both Gaussian tails and the first derivative. Its rotating finite-component error is below \(1.9\times10^{-16}\) throughout the declared sector.

Internal review and 192/256-bit outward checks passed. I updated the [progress register](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/research-progress/02_UNIFORM_ARITHMETIC_RESIDUAL_PROGRESS_20261019.md) and [round summary](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/summary/02_UNIFORM_ARITHMETIC_RESIDUAL_ROUND_SUMMARY_20261019.md).

UAR-03 is next. The complete residual bound and physical exclusion remain open.
Please proceed with UAR-03 and update the progress register and round summary.
I’ll work on UAR-03’s edge model, complete error bound, and cutoff matching, then record the result and any remaining limits in the progress register and round summary.

The edge analysis has a domain trap: the published asymptotic bound assumes the natural cutoff, while our contract also uses the neighboring frozen cutoff. I’m checking a bounded-contour model of the actual edge that works for both choices. Separately, the cutoff-matching calculation suggests the corrected jumps may have a summable allowance.

The tail bounds now support a complete edge model that agrees across same-cutoff chart overlaps. The corrected-transition calculation also gives a total allowance below \(2.639\times10^{-7}\) across the sector, avoiding the earlier divergent raw-mode payment. I’m checking the constants and proof before marking UAR-03 complete; the combined signed residual remains UAR-04’s task.

UAR-03 has passed internal proof review and the outward constant checks. I’m saving the edge-model theorem and the summable transition bound, and updating both requested documents. UAR-04 will be Ready; evaluating and bounding the retained signed integral, including numerical evaluation errors, is still outstanding.

UAR-03 is complete. The [new theorem](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/03_normalized_jet_rotation/notes/09_UNIFORM_COHERENT_EDGE_AND_CUTOFF_MATCHING_20261019.md) establishes:

- Uniform edge-model error below \(4.3\times10^{-35}\).
- Corrected-transition prefix allowance below \(2.639\times10^{-7}\).

Internal review and 192/256-bit outward checks passed.

Updated the [progress register](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/research-progress/02_UNIFORM_ARITHMETIC_RESIDUAL_PROGRESS_20261019.md) and [round summary](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/summary/02_UNIFORM_ARITHMETIC_RESIDUAL_ROUND_SUMMARY_20261019.md). UAR-04 is Ready; retained-integral evaluation, the combined signed residual bound, and physical exclusion remain open.
Excellent, please continue with UAR-04

I’ll work on UAR-04’s combined signed increment, including the retained model, every cutoff transition and the complete error allowance. I’ll compare the result in the declared norm and update the progress register and round summary.

The earlier corrected Riemann–Siegel disk estimate is a stronger comparator here than S04’s raw residual bound. I’m checking whether the signed edge estimate can improve that allowance after paying every cutoff transition; the very small UAR-02 and UAR-03 remainder bounds alone don’t settle this comparison.

A useful route has emerged: estimate the edge remainder on a wider analytic disk, using the slowly varying symmetric normalizer to control its first jet. In parallel, I’m checking whether the signed contour expansion tightens the dominant edge allowance. The comparison will include both endpoints, all cutoff prefixes and the complete remainder budget.

The finite-mode estimate now retains a useful phase cancellation: after rotation, the two channel weights add to a fixed total. The contour calculation also gives a tighter leading edge term. I’m assembling the full prefix bound and having a separate internal reviewer check the tails, normalization and comparison.

The complete bound is now below \(3.246e^{-13/(16t)}\), or \(2.846\times10^{-7}\) across the declared sector. It includes every physical prefix and cutoff switch. The internal review is checking the proof and constants; I’m preparing the progress updates. A paid nonzero anchor remains the next task.

The internal review and 192/256-bit checks passed. UAR-01 through UAR-03 still verify unchanged. I’ve saved the new theorem and records, updated the progress register and round summary, and marked UAR-05 Ready for the paid anchor and separation work.

UAR-04 is complete. The complete residual increment is bounded by **\(3.246e^{-13/(16t)}<2.846\times10^{-7}\)** across every declared prefix and cutoff transition. Internal review and 192/256-bit checks passed.

Saved the [research note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/03_normalized_jet_rotation/notes/10_UNIFORM_SIGNED_RESIDUAL_INCREMENT_20261019.md), updated the [progress register](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/research-progress/02_UNIFORM_ARITHMETIC_RESIDUAL_PROGRESS_20261019.md) and [round summary](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/summary/02_UNIFORM_ARITHMETIC_RESIDUAL_ROUND_SUMMARY_20261019.md).

**UAR-05 is Ready.** The paid nonzero anchor and physical separation remain open; no new collision exclusion is claimed.
Excellent, please proceed with UAR-05 and update the progress register and round summary.
I’ll use UAR-04’s complete increment bound to assess a paid physical anchor and the approximant’s intervening variation, then update the progress register and round summary with the reviewed outcome.

A first outward evaluation found a physical first-jet anchor near the sector’s opening height, with normalized radius about 1.544 before the small residual payment. I’m checking one closed neighborhood around it. The same-data direct endpoint test has a smaller error budget, so I’ll keep that comparison explicit.

The closed-box check is positive after paying the anchor, approximant variation and rebased residual increment: the normalized first-jet margin exceeds 0.539. This is a bounded result near the opening height; separation across the full sector remains open. The refined local transport allowance is still larger than the matched direct endpoint allowance.

The bounded certificate passed internal review. It encloses the full 22,026-mode approximation over the exact time band and spatial interval, and rejects control fixtures where anchor, variation or residual payments are omitted. I’m saving the result and marking UAR-06 Ready only for this declared box.

The UAR-05 note, progress register and round summary are saved. The new 192/256-bit receipt verifies, matches the reviewer’s replay, and leaves UAR-01 through UAR-04 valid. Full-sector separation remains open, and the matched direct test retains the stronger margin on this box.

UAR-05 is complete **for the declared bounded box**. After all errors, the first-jet margin exceeds **0.539** and normalized physical energy exceeds **0.27**. Internal review and 192/256-bit checks passed.

Saved the [research note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/03_normalized_jet_rotation/notes/11_PAID_ANCHOR_AND_BOUNDED_PHYSICAL_SEPARATION_20261019.md), and updated the [progress register](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/research-progress/02_UNIFORM_ARITHMETIC_RESIDUAL_PROGRESS_20261019.md) and [round summary](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/11_arithmetic_collision_rigidity/symmetries/summary/02_UNIFORM_ARITHMETIC_RESIDUAL_ROUND_SUMMARY_20261019.md).

**UAR-06 is Ready on this box only.** Direct endpoint certification remains stronger; full-sector separation remains open.
